predecessors.note: At Augsburg in 952 Berengar II 'had to renounce the Veronese march'; it replaced Berengar I's march of c. 890, itself 'the former Carolingian March of Friuli' (infobox: preceded by the Duchy of Friuli).

land.text: the cities of the Veronese League of 1164: Verona, Padua and Vicenza (Venice is left out)

successors.note: 1167: the Veronese cities join the Lombard League; the March of Verona page calls this 'the de facto end of the march' and says the emperors went on appointing vicars, but the office became nominal, and from the 13th century the real lords of Verona were Scaliger podestàs (Venice took most of the former march by about 1420). The Lombard League is an association (umbrella, never territory, research-brief rule 4), so the land is handed to the Cliopatria Holy Roman Empire shape, which draws north Italy, and the League stays in this note and in the 1167 war. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review): the successor was lombard-league.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no march; the Kingdom of Italy row draws all north Italy as one). The page lists the march's parts without a border: Verona, the Adige valley around Trento, Friuli around Aquileia and Istria 'attached to Verona as a county' in 952. The gazetteer shape holds the provinces of Verona, Padua and Vicenza (the Veronese League cities), Trento, Friuli and Istria; the page gives no infobox area, so no area comparison was possible. Under the dukes of Bavaria 952-975 and of Carinthia 976-1151, the march is drawn as a vassal tint of its duke.

region.text: the cities of the Veronese League of 1164: Verona, Padua and Vicenza (Venice is left out)

ledger.note: 1167: the Lombard League is formed and the march ends in fact. 'this constituted the de facto end of the march' after the Veronese League of 1164; confirmed by the Lombard victory at Legnano in 1176. From the 13th century the Scaliger podestàs ruled Verona; Venice conquered the rest by about 1420. Successor (repair of 2026-10-25): the territorial holder is holy-roman-empire; the Lombard League (umbrella) only joined the cities together. The page's infobox also lists the Patria del Friuli as a successor entity.

wars.outcome: The Veronese League of 1164 merged into the Lombard League of 1167 (oath of Pontida, 7 April 1167); the emperor's army was defeated at Legnano on 29 May 1176; the Peace of Constance of 1183 compromised.
wars.note: The March of Verona page dates only 1164, 1167 and 1176; the Peace of Constance is from the Lombard League page.

certainty.note: The page names the march's parts but fixes no border; the Adige valley grant of 1004 and the 1070 and 1077 detachments are dated, their frontiers are not.

notes:
Two pages opened (budget 2). Cliopatria has no Verona march; its Kingdom of Italy row draws north Italy. Not settled: the march's real extent (the page lists parts, not a map; Padua, Treviso and Vicenza are read in from the Veronese League; Treviso, Belluno and the rest of the Veneto are not drawn); the exact month of 952; which lord held it 976-1151 beyond 'a Carinthian march'; the Bavarian and Carinthian dossiers draw it as a vassal tint (vassal events counterpart march-of-verona). Counterparts needing dossiers: Bishopric of Trent (1004-1803), March of Istria, patriarchate-of-aquileia (Cliopatria 1260-1449, eu-13/eu-09).

Repair of 2026-10-25 (review findings): (1) the vassal events of the march's overlords are added from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord): Bavaria 952-976 and Carinthia 976-1151, the mirrors of stem-duchy-of-bavaria /ledger 952 and 976 and duchy-of-carinthia /ledger 976 and 1151; the Carinthia dossier's two events still draw the 976 extent (with Trentino, Friuli and Istria) at 1151, which is stale. (2) The successor is holy-roman-empire (territorial) instead of the umbrella lombard-league; kingdom-of-italy (eu-13) draws nothing between 970 and 1861 in Cliopatria, and the Cliopatria Holy Roman Empire shape (1167) holds Verona, Padua and Vicenza. The March of Verona page was re-read; its infobox lists the Patria del Friuli and the Lombard League as successors, and it gives no ruler of the territory 1167-1250 beyond nominal vicars and the Scaliger from the 13th century (Ezzelino 1223-1233 in its rulers list). (3) Routing: patriarchate-of-aquileia (Cliopatria 1260-1449, eu-13) must start in 1077 for the /ledger/3 loss of Friuli.
